bib.title: HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 4791-4800

read.skipped: The PDF has no supplemental appendix (BERT hyperparameters, AF setup, agreement estimation are referred to as 'Supp A' / 'the appendix' but are not in the file).

question: Is commonsense natural language inference actually solved by deep pretrained models like BERT, or did SWAG only reward dataset-specific artifacts?
hypothesis: BERT's SWAG success comes from picking up distributional biases in machine-generated endings, so a dataset rebuilt by Adversarial Filtering with stronger generators and discriminators will stay hard for models while easy for humans.
contributions: Analysis of why BERT solved SWAG (ending-only, shuffled ablations, AF with different generators)
HellaSwag, a 70k-example four-way commonsense NLI benchmark built with Adversarial Filtering over ActivityNet and WikiHow
Evidence of a 'Goldilocks zone' of generation length where text is nonsensical to humans yet fools discriminators
Argument for benchmarks that co-evolve adversarially with the state of the art

method.summary: The authors ablate BERT-Large on SWAG, then build HellaSwag by running Adversarial Filtering with GPT as the ending generator and BERT-Large as the discriminator over ActivityNet Captions and WikiHow, followed by crowd validation. Baselines from fastText to BERT-Large are fine-tuned with four-way cross-entropy and compared with five-worker majority-vote humans.
method.task: Commonsense NLI: choose the true continuation among four endings

datasets.name: HellaSwag
datasets.size: 70k examples (25k ActivityNet contexts, 45k WikiHow contexts); validation 10K, test 10K; 5K in-domain and 5K zero-shot per set
datasets.split: Table 1 splits: Overall 10K val/10K test; In-Domain 5K/5K; Zero-Shot 5K/5K; ActivityNet 3.2K/3.5K; WikiHow 6.8K/6.5K
datasets.source: ActivityNet Captions (Krishna et al. 2017) and 80k scraped WikiHow context/follow-up paragraphs; licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: WikiHow contexts at most three sentences, follow-ups two sentences; endings generated by finetuned GPT, filtered with AF using BERT-Large; human validation with six endings (one true, five from AF), rated-realistic generations replaced over several rounds; keep best-agreement contexts

datasets.name: SWAG
datasets.preprocessing: Ablations: Ending Only, Shuffled, Shuffled+Ending Only

models.name: BERT-Large
models.architecture: bidirectional transformer, fine-tuned end to end
models.init_from: pretrained BERT-Large checkpoint (re-initialized each AF iteration)

other.note: Paper says 3x the parameters of BERT-Base

other.also_used: fine-tuned GPT is the ending generator for HellaSwag

models.name: ESIM+ELMo
models.architecture: best ELMo NLI model, final layer four-way softmax over endings

models.name: LSTM sentence encoder (GloVe / ELMo / frozen BERT-Base embeddings)
models.architecture: randomly initialized two-layer bi-LSTM, second layer max-pooled into an MLP giving a logit

other.embedding_note: for ELMo and BERT-Base the model learns scalar weights over internal layers

training.objective: four-way cross-entropy over endings; each model maps (context, ending) to a logit (fastText: binary cross entropy)

other.note: Hyperparameters deferred to an appendix not present in the PDF

inference.decoding: GPT generates candidate endings (decoding settings not stated); classifiers pick the highest-logit ending
inference.samples: human: five independent crowd workers per item, majority vote; model runs/seeds not stated

parameters.AF: iterative: random Dtrain/Dtest partition each iteration, classifier trained on Dtrain to tell real vs generated, easy generations in Dtest replaced; repeated until adversary accuracy converges
parameters.ending_length: two sentences chosen (one and three also tested)

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of four-way multiple-choice items answered correctly

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers on val and test; no seeds or significance tests stated. Chance is 25.0. Zero-shot sets use held-out categories.

evidence.quote: asking five independent crowd workers to solve

results.claim: Humans score over 95% on HellaSwag while the best model, BERT-Large, scores 47.3% overall on test.
results.quote: it still performs the strongest at 47.3% overall
results.table: Table 1, row BERT-Large, column Overall Test

results.claim: Human accuracy on the HellaSwag test set.
results.setup: HellaSwag test overall, five crowd workers, majority vote

results.claim: ESIM+ELMo reached 59% on SWAG but only 33.3% on HellaSwag.
results.quote: it obtains only 33.3% accuracy on HellaSwag

results.claim: BERT-Large on SWAG with context removed (Ending Only) drops 11.9 points.
With context removed and endings shuffled, BERT still gets 60.4% on SWAG, above ELMo's roughly 60%.
Zero-shot categories cost BERT-Large about 5 points on test relative to in-domain.
results.table: Table 1, row BERT-Large, column Zero-Shot Test

results.claim: WikiHow is much harder for models than ActivityNet: BERT-Large about 45% vs humans 96.5%.
results.table: Table 1, row BERT-Large, column WikiHow Test

results.claim: BERT-Large trained on SWAG scores only 34.6% on HellaSwag.
results.setup: Validation sets, trained on SWAG, evaluated on HellaSwag overall

results.claim: Training on SWAG and testing on HellaSwag lowers performance by 12%; the reverse by 15%.
AF with SWAG's original LSTM generator converges at roughly 75% BERT-Large accuracy, while GPT generations push it below 30%.
AF on WikiHow with GPT converges near 35%, 40% and 50% for one-, two- and three-sentence endings; two sentences chosen.
Ending-length effect: WikiHow 2-sentence generations average 41 tokens vs 13 for ActivityNet.
A discriminator with 3x the parameters of the adversarial filter (BERT-Large vs BERT-Base) still reaches only 63%.
results.setup: WikiHow AF ablation, no human validation

results.claim: Extrapolating a log-linear fit, human-level HellaSwag would need about 10^9 GPU-hours of pretraining (over 100k GPU years).
results.setup: Rough estimate converting reported TPU runtimes to RTX 2080 Ti via roofline model

results.claim: Freezing BERT-Base under an LSTM lowers overall performance by 4.3%.

limits: Hyperparameters, AF details and agreement estimation are in a supplement not in this PDF.
Ceiling by design: filtered against BERT-Large, so model ranking against the filter is biased.
No seeds or significance tests; GPU-hour extrapolation is rough.
Authors concede the task, not the dataset, is the target and that future models may only exploit new spurious patterns.
Dated: GPT-4-class models later scored above 90%.

terms.definition: iteratively train discriminators to separate real from generated endings and replace easily classified generations with adversarial ones
text complexity where generations are nonsensical to humans yet state-of-the-art discriminators cannot tell the difference

lineage.note: HellaSwag is the next iteration of SWAG with AF

lineage.work: Gururangan et al. 2018; Poliak et al. 2018
